commits.message:
feat(email-parsing): expand skills taxonomy, fix skill/work-auth/LinkedIn/signature extraction gaps

Answers the "is the taxonomy auto-updated" question with a fix, not
just an answer: it wasn't, and worse, the taxonomy that was hooked up
to actual skill extraction (skills.json, ~33 terms) and the richer one
with categories/aliases/related_skills (canonical_skills.json, ~35
terms) were two separately-maintained near-duplicates of the same
generic software-engineering seed list -- neither had ever been
expanded for the IT-staffing/recruiting domain Hermes actually parses
in production. Real postings mentioning Amazon Connect, TIBCO
BusinessWorks, SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow, etc. matched almost
nothing no matter which file a given code path happened to read.

Taxonomy changes:
- canonical_skills.json: 35 -> 181 entries, adding IT-staffing/
  enterprise coverage (AWS/Azure specific services, ERP/CRM systems,
  BI/reporting tools, integration middleware, testing/ITSM tools,
  mainframe, security/identity, mobile, ML libraries). Every new
  related_skills reference resolves to a real canonical name and no
  alias collides with another skill's -- verified against the
  existing (previously never-run-in-CI) hermes-400-taxonomy-
  validation.py, which also caught and fixed 6 pre-existing dangling
  related_titles references in job_titles.json that predate this
  change.
- job_titles.json: 14 -> 43 entries, same domain gap (.NET Developer,
  Business Analyst, Project Manager, Solutions Architect, SAP/
  Salesforce/ServiceNow titles, data/ML roles, infra roles).
- skills.json deleted; loader.py now points load_skills_taxonomy()
  (and therefore extract_skills(), the actual required/preferred-
  skill matcher for parsed emails) at canonical_skills.json instead --
  one source of truth for both extraction and normalization, not two
  drifting copies. skill_aliases.json/title_aliases.json left alone
  (other consumers not fully audited this pass); no new collisions
  against them.

Bugs fixed, each confirmed against real production drafts:

- extract_labeled_section() (required/preferred skills) required an
  exact "Nice to Have:" match -- real postings write "Nice to have
  skills:" (extra word before the colon), which silently matched
  nothing. Also returned only the first line of a section via
  clean_field(), truncating a real multi-bullet preferred-skills list
  to its first bullet even once the label matched.
- Work authorization only recognized immigration-status terms (H1B,
  Green Card, OPT, ...) -- added "Independent Visa" and "no
  sponsorship" staffing-industry phrasing, which was simply absent.
- LinkedIn URL extraction (extract_linkedin_url) already existed but
  was only wired into resume parsing -- added to job-requirement
  records and provenance/frontend display.
- Signature parser's quoted-history boundary (Phase 6) correctly
  protects a stale signature ten replies deep in a real thread, but
  had no concept of "this message IS a single forward in its
  entirety" -- for that shape (extremely common for job-board-
  forwarded postings), there is no fresh content above the boundary
  to protect, yet the recruiter's own name/company/email sits exactly
  where search stopped. Added a narrow pure-forward path: skip past
  the forwarded header block itself (not into it, where the header's
  own duplicate "Subject:" line was getting misread as a job title),
  then try a head-window scan there before falling back to the
  original tail-window/signoff-marker logic untouched. Verified the
  original protection still holds for genuine multi-reply quoted
  history.

New coverage:
- hermes-850-email-signature-check.py: this parser (662 lines of
  heuristics) had zero regression tests before this change.
- hermes-850-email-parsing-check.py: extended the real-forwarded-
  posting fixture with work-authorization phrasing, a bare LinkedIn
  URL, and IT-staffing-domain skill terms in both required and
  preferred sections.

Verified: full hermes-850-*/hermes-400-*/hermes-450-channel-intake-
check.py regression suite green against a freshly reset schema, plus
hermes-400-taxonomy-validation.py (structural taxonomy integrity) and
a direct resume-parsing check (unaffected by the JD-side changes).
Re-tested live against the three real production drafts already
flagged this session -- required/preferred skills now correctly
surface domain-specific terms (TIBCO BusinessWorks, Azure Integration
Services, Amazon Connect/Lex, DynamoDB, ...), work_authorization now
resolves "Independent Visa" instead of null, and the signature parser
now runs (and recovers the sender's real email) instead of silently
returning nothing for every job-board forward.

Known remaining gap, not chased further this pass: one specific
vendor's emails render each signature token on its own line ("From:
/ / Harry, / / ITECSUS / / harry@itecsus.com") after HTML->text
conversion, unusual enough that name/company extraction still misses
there even with detection now running. spaCy is already an installed
dependency (used today only as a blank tokenizer) -- downloading
en_core_web_sm (~13MB, not a new package) to add real NER as a
secondary signal for exactly this kind of free-form signature block
is a reasonable next iteration, deferred rather than rushed into this
already-large change.
